judgement.summary:
Step 3 is NOT yet acceptable, but nothing that ships is wrong. I reproduced the suite exactly as the scope documents it (348 passed, 3 failed — test_config_resolution ×2 and test_embedding_provider_refactor::test_fireworks_qwen, all API-key/config environment), and I could not find an unsound path in the production code: `on_answer`'s three guards, `start_gate`'s counter pairing, `_gate`'s capture-and-compare, `_write`, `_first_failure`, `_stop_if_cancelled` and `Gate_Writer.put_interpretation` all do what the plan says. What is wrong is the evidence around the code and four sentences of the plan.

The serious half is test adequacy, and I measured it rather than argued it. I rebound the PRODUCTION methods from a pytest plugin (no file on disk touched) and re-ran the whole scope suite. Removing `self.gate_started()` from `InterpretationTask.start_gate`: 348 passed, 3 failed — byte-identical to the clean baseline. Removing the whole `except BaseException: gate_finished(); coro.close(); raise` compensation: identical. Removing `on_answer`'s `if self.state[idx] == _GATING: return` — the D11 clause the entire re-design turns on: identical. Three settled rulings (two clauses of F4, and D11's running-gate branch) are pinned by nothing at all. The reason is a single shape: both test doubles in `archive/tests/test_interpretation_driver.py` override `start_gate` instead of the gate's body, and `_TaskGroupGateTask.start_gate` (:265-278) is a verbatim nine-line re-typing of production :570-585 with one line swapped — so the assertions that look like they pin F4 run against the copy, and the docstring at :258-259 claims the opposite ("The production `start_gate` ... is what runs for that entry" — it does not). That is the copy-paste-and-modify the project's reuse rule names, and it is why the mutations survive. The elegant repair is one seam lower: production `start_gate` resolves `_gate` from module globals at call time (:577), so a test can swap the gate BODY (`monkeypatch.setattr(SI, "_gate", ...)`) and let the shipped starter run. That also opens a real `_GATING` window, which is exactly what the missing D11 test needs.

I confirmed the `_GATING` branch is live in step 3, not a step-5 concern: `mk_answer_tool`'s handler loops over `args["interpretations"]` with no await between items (:737-757), so two items naming one entry in ONE tool call hit it. My probe on the on-disk code: one gate, judging the newer text. With the guard removed: two gate tasks for one entry, i.e. two `put_interpretation` transactions and two `invalidate_vectors` — and in step 5, two judge sessions and a possible double mint.

The other half is four false sentences in plan rev 5.3, all of which the code is on the right side of. §15.11:1522 "Behaviour equals today's with three exceptions" is the step-3 acceptance criterion and it is not exhaustive: HEAD's `_run_agent` re-enters at `task.batches[0]` from all four recovering arms (HEAD:755, :822, :827, :841, :862) and re-writes already-answered entries through an unconditional `Semantic_DB[key] = SemanticRecord(...)` (HEAD:381-402), while the new loop resumes from `unanswered_in_batch()`; the throttle sleeps also went from flat 1200/2 s to jittered-and-backed-off, and the recursion became a loop. All three are prescribed by §5.3 and §15.4 — only §15.11's count is wrong. §15.2:948 and §15.6:1254 still declare `retry_prompt(self, missing, chunk)` where the code takes one parameter (and §15.3:994-997 already prescribes the one-parameter split, so the code is right and only the two signature rows are stale). §15.10:1470 claims the legacy-arity parametrisation "moves here" onto the `put_interpretation` tests; it did not move, and I measured that it should not: seeding a record at n = 12, 13, 14, 15 and putting over it produces four identical 15-field records, so the ordered parametrisation would be one assertion run four times.

Every remaining item is a test edit or a plan edit. No production code change is required, and I found no hack in the shipped code.

rulings.title: §15.11's "behaviour equals today's with three exceptions" is not exhaustive: a recycle no longer re-sends batch 0 (nor are the throttle sleeps or the recursion today's)
rulings.rationale: Verified on both sides myself. HEAD: `git show HEAD:Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py` has `_run_agent` start at `first_prompt, task.batch_range = task.batches[0]` (HEAD:755) and all four recovering arms `return await _run_agent(...)` (HEAD:822, :827, :841, :862), the batch prompts are pre-built strings (HEAD:1160), and `write_answer` (HEAD:381-402) writes `Semantic_DB[key] = SemanticRecord(...)` unconditionally — so a recycle really did re-ask and re-write already-answered entries, vector invalidation included. Working tree: `next_batch` (:403-415) starts from `unanswered_in_batch()` = `[i for i in self.batch if self.state[i] == _SENT]` (:416-417), so `_GATING`/`_DONE` entries are structurally excluded. That is a real, store-visible behaviour change and it is not among §15.11's three. The challenger's addition also checks out: HEAD:818-827 sleeps a flat 1200 s / 2 s and recurses, while :1039-1049 jitters (1200 ± 60) and backs off (min(2·2**throttled, 60) × U(0.5,1.5)) inside a `while True`. So the sentence is short by three, not one. The code is right — §5.3 "Recycle paths" (:277-281), §15.4's closing "Recycle:" paragraph (:1089-1091) and §15.4's three prescribed changes (:1052-1073) all order exactly what shipped — and §15.11 is the one sentence that contradicts them. §15.11 is the step-3 acceptance criterion the scope names, which is why a stale sentence there is worth a ruling rather than a shrug; minor because no behaviour, test or decision changes.
rulings.fix: Plan edit only, by hand (no scripted edits to plan documents). At SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1522, stop counting. The sentence is doing two jobs — certifying what reaches the STORE and summarising how the session loop changed — and only the first can honestly be an exhaustive short list. Rewrite it in substance as: what reaches the store is today's with two exceptions — every interpretation write (an answer's and a D11 correction's alike) is a task of the run's task group, so a write that fails now fails the run where today a failed correction escaped the tool handler as an opaque tool error and the run still succeeded; and on the success path a correction's write is no longer synchronous with the tool reply, landing at the handler's next `await` (`await _report(...)`), still before the reply reaches the agent. Then say the session loop itself is the new one of §5.3/§15.4 rather than today's, and point at those sections instead of re-listing: one turn per batch; a recycle or throttle retry resumes from the entries still `_SENT` instead of re-sending the pre-built batch-0 prompt in full (today's `_run_agent` re-enters at `task.batches[0]`), so answered entries are neither re-asked nor re-written; the throttle sleeps jitter and back off; the handlers loop rather than recurse. Keep the closing "The closing line still counts entities, not writes." No code and no test change: `test_poisoned_session_recycles_a_fresh_driver_and_keeps_answers` (test_interpretation_driver.py:236-251) already pins the recycle resumption on the poisoned-session arm.

rulings.title: The driver tests replace production `start_gate` with a verbatim copy, so ruling F4 is pinned by nothing — I removed the counter increment and the compensation from the shipped method and the whole suite stayed green
rulings.rationale: I reproduced the mutations myself rather than trusting the report. With a pytest plugin rebinding `SI.InterpretationTask.start_gate` at `pytest_configure` (no file modified), over the full scope suite: baseline 3 failed / 348 passed; drop `self.gate_started()` → 3 failed / 348 passed; drop the entire `except BaseException: self.gate_finished(); coro.close(); raise` → 3 failed / 348 passed; move `gate_started()` after `create_task` (over the three step-3 files) → 54 passed. Byte-identical to clean in every case. The cause is visible by reading: `_RecordingTask.start_gate` (test_interpretation_driver.py:53-55) replaces the method wholesale, and `_TaskGroupGateTask.start_gate` (:265-278) re-types production :570-585 line for line with only `coro = _gate(self, idx)` swapped for `coro = self._gate_body()` — so `assert task.gates_running == 0` at :323, :394 and the wait-for-gate test all assert about the copy, and production `InterpretationTask.start_gate` is never entered from that module. The docstring at :258-259 states the opposite of what happens ("The production `start_gate` (counter paired to the task, compensation when the group refuses it) is what runs for that entry"), and the two properties it names in that parenthesis are precisely the two nothing tests; `slow_idx` at :256 names no parameter (`__init__` takes `idx`). Nine identical lines in two places with only one of them tested is exactly the copy-paste-and-modify the project's reuse rule forbids, and F4 is one of the settled rulings this re-review exists to check. Major, at the low end: the shipped method on disk is correct, so this is test adequacy plus duplication, not a defect. I trim the finding's own claim that its fix makes mutations (a)-(c) fail — (b) and (c) live only on the `create_task`-refusal edge, which no existing test reaches (`test_a_cancelled_session_is_not_recycled...` :363-397 re-raises in `_stop_if_cancelled` before a second turn, so `create_task` is never called on an aborting group), so one further test is required.
rulings.fix: Swap the gate BODY, not the starter, and add the refusal test. (1) Delete `_TaskGroupGateTask` (:255-278) and `_RecordingTask`'s `start_gate` override (:53-55). Production `start_gate` resolves `_gate` from module globals at call time (semantic_interpretation.py:577), so each test that needs a special gate does `monkeypatch.setattr(SI, "_gate", dispatch)` with a dispatcher that returns the recording coroutine for ordinary entries and the supplied body for the special one; every driver test then runs the shipped starter. (2) With `_RecordingTask` no longer needing a group-free path, collapse `_run` (:142-146) and `_run_in_group` (:281-294) into one runner that always wraps `_run_agent` in an `asyncio.TaskGroup` and does the select-inside / raise-outside dance — which is what `interpret_file` always does. (3) Add one test for F4's compensation clause, which (1) alone does not reach: inside a task group whose `create_task` is made to raise, one `on_answer` must leave `gates_running == 0` and must have closed the never-started coroutine (assert on the coroutine's `cr_frame is None`, and/or run under `warnings.simplefilter("error")` so 'coroutine was never awaited' fails the test). (4) Fix the prose at :256-259: delete the false sentence and the `slow_idx` name (it falls out for free if the class is deleted). Two existing tests assert `task.written` synchronously and will need one `await asyncio.sleep(0)` between the answer and the assertion once the gate is a real task — `test_the_answer_tool_reports_the_batch_and_refuses_unknown_entries` (:183) and `test_a_correction_gates_again_and_an_identical_resubmission_does_nothing` (:191-206, which additionally needs the yield BETWEEN the first answer and the correction so the correction finds the entry `_DONE` rather than `_GATING`); that is the production sequencing §15.5's concurrency paragraph rests on, which the synchronous stub currently hides. ACCEPTANCE GATE, and it is objective: with the fix applied, each of the four F4 mutations — no `gate_started()`; `gate_started()` after `create_task`; no `except BaseException` compensation; no `add_done_callback` — must fail at least one test by ASSERTION (today only the fourth is detected, and only as a hang). Test shapes beyond that gate are the implementer's call (settled).

rulings.title: `on_answer`'s `_GATING` early return — the D11 clause the re-design turns on — has zero coverage and is reachable in step 3 through the answer handler's own synchronous item loop
rulings.rationale: Verified three ways on the code on disk. Reachability: `mk_answer_tool`'s handler iterates `args["interpretations"]` with no await anywhere between :737 and :757 (the first await is `await _report(...)` at :764), and `task._label_to_idx.get(key)` at :744 maps two items with the same type+name to one index — so item 1 sets `_GATING` (:598) and creates a gate task that has not run yet, and item 2 lands on :596-597. My probe against the unmodified module (real `InterpretationTask` in an `asyncio.TaskGroup`, `SI._gate` stubbed to record, one `answer` call carrying `[{T.c0: 'first'}, {T.c0: 'second'}]`): `gates started: [(0, 'second')]` — one gate, on the newest text, exactly D11. This is NOT the case §15.10 defers to step 5 ("a correction that lands during the judge session"); it needs no judge, only two items in one JSON array. Coverage: `_RecordingTask.start_gate` sets `_DONE` synchronously (test_interpretation_driver.py:53-55), so `_GATING` never persists in any driver test — including the sole correction test (:195-207, `_DONE → _GATING → _DONE`); the storage tests set `state[i] = _GATING` by hand and call `_gate` directly, never `on_answer`. Load-bearing: with the guard removed (plugin rebinding `on_answer`, no file modified) the same probe gives `gates started: [(0, 'second'), (0, 'second')]` — two gate tasks for one entry, hence two `Gate_Writer.put_interpretation` transactions and two `invalidate_vectors` (semantics.py:952-973) — and the full scope suite comes back 3 failed / 348 passed, byte-identical to clean. Major for what the branch protects: FIX_LIST's open question 1 (:83-87) rests the whole "two gates for one entity never overlap" warrant on `on_answer` observing state synchronously, and this guard is half of that mechanism; in step 5 losing it is two judge sessions (8-20 s, ≈$0.13 each) on one entity and two concurrent mint decisions. The step-3 blast radius is duplicated work, not corruption — the corruption case is step 5 — but the settled delegation of test CHOICES to the implementer does not cover an untested branch when the scope makes "are the tests adequate?" an explicit question and §15.10's step-3 list enumerates only the two `_DONE`-path corrections.
rulings.fix: Add one step-3 test beside the existing correction test at test_interpretation_driver.py:195: one `answer` tool call carrying two items for the SAME entry with DIFFERENT texts, inside a task group, asserting that exactly one gate ran and that it saw the second text (assert the recorded list equals `["second wording"]` — a list, not a length, so the assertion pins both "one gate" and D11's actual promise that the running gate picks the newer text up). Two traps to avoid, both real: do not build it from the `_answer(0, 0)` helper (:115-124), whose translation is derived from the index, so both items would carry identical text and the byte-identical guard at :594 would swallow the second before the `_GATING` branch is reached — the test would then pass against the mutated code too; and the entry must genuinely be `_GATING` when the second item arrives, which it is today under `_TaskGroupGateTask` and will be under F-A's `_gate`-body swap. ACCEPTANCE GATE: removing `if self.state[idx] == _GATING: return` from `InterpretationTask.on_answer` must fail this test. Plan edit, by hand: §15.10's step-3 bullet (c) currently lists only the two `_DONE`-path corrections; add the third — two items for one entry in one `answer` call run one gate, on the newer text — and say it is reachable in step 3 through the handler's synchronous item loop, so it is not the step-5 case the step-5 bullet defers.

rulings.title: §15.10 claims the legacy-arity parametrisation moved onto the `put_interpretation` tests; it did not — but I measured that it should not, because on that path it is n-invariant
rulings.rationale: Half stands, half I reject, and I measured both. STANDS: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1470 states the `@pytest.mark.parametrize("n", [12, 13, 14, 15])` legacy-arity coverage of the interpretation write path "moves here from the deleted `update_interpretation` tests". It did not. The only parametrize in the module is test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:158, over `test_gate_write_on_a_legacy_arity_record`, whose body calls `w.update_gate_fields(...)` (:164); the four `put_interpretation` tests (:241, :258, :268, :284) carry none, and `_write_raw` — the only way to seed a legacy-arity record — is called at just :161 and :371. So a plan sentence asserts something about the tests that is false. §10:697's "through both writers" is the same claim, also unsatisfied. REJECTED: the finding's prescribed remedy, and its rationale for it. `put_interpretation` (semantics.py:952-973) names all 13 wire+gate fields into `_put_fields`, which does `self._decode(raw)._replace(**fields)` (semantics.py:838) after `_decode` pads a short tuple to 15 — and the three fields a legacy packing truncates (position, from_collection, baseline_interpretation, indices 12-14) are three of the fields `put_interpretation` writes explicitly. I ran it: seeding the same record at n = 12, 13, 14, 15 and putting over it gives four identical records, every one 15 fields, with position, from_collection and baseline filled and experience/goal_patterns carried up. So the ordered parametrisation is one assertion run four times — zero discriminating power, and a duplicate assertion is the inelegant option the project rules reject. Contrast :167-168 in the test it would be copied from, where `got.position == (... if n >= 13 else None)` genuinely varies with n, because `update_gate_fields` inherits those fields instead of writing them. The finding's aside that the existing test runs [12, 13, 14] rather than [12, 13, 14, 15] is a misfire: §10:697 specifies those three as inputs with "15 read back" (asserted at :170), and n = 15 as an input is today's encoder, already pinned at :122-129. Minor, and lower than the finding implies: what the (arity-independent) hole actually leaves unpinned is the copy-up of `experience`/`goal_patterns`, and those belong to experience-memory records — `_NON_INTERPRETABLE_KINDS` at semantic_interpretation.py:128 excludes `EntityKind.EXPERIENCE`, so an interpreted entity never carries them and the copy-up is defensive, not load-bearing on live data.
rulings.fix: Plan edit by hand, and it is the mandatory half: at SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1470 delete the claim that the parametrisation moves onto `put_interpretation`, and say what is true instead — the legacy-arity parametrisation stays on `update_gate_fields`, where the assertion depends on n because that writer inherits `position`/`from_collection` from the stored record, while `put_interpretation` writes all three formerly-truncated fields itself and is therefore arity-invariant; the interpretation write path keeps its 15-field round trip through the existing `assert _raw_len(k) == 15` at :256. Make the same correction at §10:697 ("through both writers"). Do NOT add the parametrisation (measured: four identical records). This supersedes the clause of FIX_LIST open question 4 that ordered it — its stated rationale ("cheap insurance") is void on this path, and test shapes are the implementer's per the settled list. Optional, and worth one line if the implementer wants it: an unparametrised `put_interpretation` test that seeds a 12-field raw record with `experience`/`goal_patterns` set and asserts they survive the put while `position` is rewritten — that has real discriminating power (it fails if those two names are added to `_put_fields`'s dict), which the ordered parametrisation does not.

rulings.title: §15.2's and §15.6's `retry_prompt(self, missing, chunk)` rows are stale — the code's one-parameter version is the right one, and §15.3 already prescribes it
rulings.rationale: Half stands. STANDS: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:948 declares `def retry_prompt(self, missing: list[int], chunk: list[int]) -> str`, while the shipped abstract (semantic_interpretation.py:468) and concrete (:663) methods both take one parameter and `_retry_unanswered` calls `task.retry_prompt(chunk)` (:990) with `chunk = task.unanswered_in_batch()` (:967). Flat contradiction, and the code is on the right side of it — not merely because the plan is stale, but because §15.3:994-997 ITSELF prescribes the one-parameter shape: it hands the run-wide unanswered set to `retry_report` and `unanswered_failure` and names the chunk `retry_prompt` re-asks as `unanswered_in_batch()`. So this is an internal plan contradiction already resolved in the code's favour by the neighbouring section, not a silent deviation. The challenger's addition checks out and the finding missed it: :1254 in §15.6's `JudgeTask` sketch carries the same stale two-parameter signature, so fixing only :948 leaves the plan self-inconsistent for step 5's judge task. REJECTED: the finding's second charge, that §15.3's "carry today's three wordings" is now false. The wording IS carried — :670-676 is the old header sentence plus the same two closing sentences, with only the number filling one slot changed — and §12 #14/#15 are the host warning line and the give-up error, neither of which is the agent-facing retry prompt, so the clause cannot bind it. I also reject the finding's stated reason for dropping the "here are the first N" clause ("can never apply"): `unanswered_in_batch` filters `self.batch` while `unanswered()` scans every state, so with a queue longer than one batch the run-wide count exceeds the chunk routinely. The clause is undesirable, not unreachable — a retry turn must not announce entries the agent has never been sent — and stating it as unreachable would invite a future author to reinstate the two-parameter form the moment they notice the counts differ. Minor, documentation only; no test pins either number (test_interpretation_driver.py:216-221 asserts the phrase and the entry text, no count).
rulings.fix: Plan edits only, by hand, at two sites. (1) SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:948 — `def retry_prompt(self, missing: list[int], chunk: list[int]) -> str` becomes `def retry_prompt(self, chunk: list[int]) -> str`. (2) SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1254 — `def retry_prompt(self, missing, chunk): -> "You have not reported a verdict. ..."` becomes `def retry_prompt(self, chunk): -> "You have not reported a verdict. ..."`, so §15.6's JudgeTask sketch still matches the base class. Do NOT rewrite §15.3:994-997 as the finding proposes — it already prescribes the shipped shape and its "three wordings" claim is true. If the implementer wants the reason on the record where the parameter used to be, one clause after "the chunk it re-asks is `unanswered_in_batch()`" saying that the chunk's own count is the number `retry_prompt` shows, because a retry turn must not name entries the agent has never been sent (the run-wide m stays on the host line, §12 #14) — but that is optional prose, not a defect fix. No code change.

findings.title: §15.11's "behaviour equals today's with three exceptions" is short by one: a recycle no longer re-sends batch 0
findings.location: ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1519-1531 (§15.11 step-3 bullet); Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:1019-1034 vs HEAD's semantic_interpretation.py:755 and :822/:827/:841/:862
findings.claim: Today (HEAD) every recovering arm of `_run_agent` does `return await _run_agent(make_driver, depth)`, and `_run_agent`'s first statement is `first_prompt, task.batch_range = task.batches[0]` — so after a rate limit, a usage cap, a poisoned session or an unexpected transport failure, the fresh session is re-sent the WHOLE of batch 0, already-answered entries included (and `task.current_batch` is not reset, so the tool-reply batch delivery then jumps forward). The new loop instead `continue`s and calls `next_batch()`, which re-sends only the entries still `_SENT` and leaves `_GATING`/`_DONE` alone. That is a real, observable behaviour change — redundant LLM re-interpretation and redundant record writes after every throttle or recycle disappear — and it is prescribed by §5.3 "Recycle paths", but it is not one of the three exceptions §15.11 lists, and §15.11 is the step-3 acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: `git show HEAD:Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py | grep -n 'first_prompt, task.batch_range\|return await _run_agent'` → :755 and the four recursion sites :822, :827, :841, :862; the diff hunk at working_tree_v2.diff:724+ shows the same. On the new side, `next_batch()` (:403-415) starts from `unanswered_in_batch()` = `[i for i in self.batch if self.state[i] == _SENT]`. Confirmed by driving `interpret_file` with a script [answer(0)], [raise PoisonedSessionError], [answer(1), correct(0)]: the second session's prompt contains only entry 1 (state trace `[_GATING, _SENT]` at the recycle), and entry 0 is written exactly once, with the corrected text.
findings.fix: Add a fourth clause to §15.11's step-3 bullet: a recycle or throttle retry now resumes from the entries still unanswered instead of re-sending batch 0 in full, so already-answered entries are neither re-asked nor re-written. (`test_poisoned_session_recycles_a_fresh_driver_and_keeps_answers` at test_interpretation_driver.py:236-251 already pins the new behaviour; only the plan text is short.)

findings.title: The driver tests replace production `start_gate` with a verbatim copy, so F4's ruling is pinned by nothing — three mutations of it leave the whole step-3 suite green
findings.claim: `_RecordingTask` and `_TaskGroupGateTask` both OVERRIDE `InterpretationTask.start_gate`. `_TaskGroupGateTask` re-types production's body line for line (`assert task_group is not None` / `gate_started()` / `try: create_task` / `except BaseException: gate_finished(); coro.close(); raise` / `add_done_callback`) with only the coroutine swapped, and its docstring at :258-259 asserts the opposite of what happens: "The production `start_gate` (counter paired to the task, compensation when the group refuses it) is what runs for that entry." It does not run — the copy does. Consequence: every F4 property (increment BEFORE `create_task`; compensate + `coro.close()` when the group refuses the task; the counter paired to the task) is asserted only about the test's private copy, so a regression in the shipped method is invisible. This is also the copy-paste-and-modify the project rule forbids: the same nine lines now live in two places and only one of them is tested.
findings.evidence: Mutation of the PRODUCTION method only (a pytest plugin that rebinds `SI.InterpretationTask.start_gate` at `pytest_configure`; no file was modified), run over `archive/tests/test_interpretation_driver.py archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py archive/tests/test_interpretation_mcp_server.py` (baseline: 54 passed): (a) drop `self.gate_started()` entirely → 54 passed; (b) move `self.gate_started()` to AFTER `create_task` → 54 passed; (c) drop the `except BaseException: gate_finished(); coro.close(); raise` compensation → 54 passed. Only dropping `add_done_callback` is detected, and then not by an assertion but by a hang: the storage module's `test_interpret_file_writes_every_answer_through_its_gate` parks in `wait_for_progress` for ever (killed at the 45 s timeout). The assertions that look like they pin this (`assert task.gates_running == 0` at :318, :390, :420; `test_the_loop_waits_for_a_gate_that_outlives_the_queue`) all run against `_TaskGroupGateTask.start_gate`, i.e. the copy — production `InterpretationTask.start_gate` is never called anywhere in test_interpretation_driver.py.
findings.fix: Swap the gate BODY, not the starter. `start_gate` resolves `_gate` from module globals at call time (`coro = _gate(self, idx)`, :578), so a test can `monkeypatch.setattr(SI, "_gate", dispatcher)` where `dispatcher(task, idx)` returns the recording coroutine for ordinary entries and the supplied body for the special one; then `_TaskGroupGateTask` disappears, `_RecordingTask` overrides nothing of production, and both `_run` and `_run_in_group` collapse into one runner that always wraps `_run_agent` in an `asyncio.TaskGroup` (which production always does). Every driver test then exercises the shipped `start_gate`, and mutations (a)-(c) fail. Also delete the false sentence at :258-259 (and the docstring's `slow_idx`, which is really the parameter `idx`).

findings.title: `on_answer`'s `_GATING` early return — the D11 clause the whole re-design turns on — has zero coverage and is reachable in step 3; deleting it leaves the suite green while starting two gates for one entry
findings.claim: D11 (plan §2, §5.4 Corrections, §15.3) says a correction arriving while an entity's gate is running is picked up by that gate and starts nothing. That branch is live in step 3 — `mk_answer_tool`'s handler calls `task.on_answer` in a plain `for` loop with NO await between items (:734-757), so two items naming the same entry in ONE `answer` call hit it: the first sets `_GATING` and creates the gate task, which has not run yet when the second arrives. rebuttals.reasoning:
I tried to refute this on three fronts and it survives all three; if anything it understates the gap.

(1) Is the HEAD behaviour really "re-send batch 0 in full"? Yes. `git show HEAD:…/semantic_interpretation.py` has `_run_agent`'s body start with `first_prompt, task.batch_range = task.batches[0]` (HEAD:755) followed unconditionally by `await driver.run_turn(first_prompt)` (HEAD:760), and the batch prompts are PRE-BUILT strings fixed at scan time (HEAD:1159-1162 `task.batches.append((task.build_prompt(...), batch_range))`), so nothing filters out entries already answered. All four recovering arms re-enter through that line (HEAD:822, :827, :841, :862). The answers that come back are written unconditionally — `write_answer` (HEAD:381-402) does a plain `Semantic_DB[key] = SemanticRecord(...)` with no "already written" test — so a recycle really does buy redundant LLM interpretation plus redundant record writes (and, through `put_interpretation`'s `invalidate_vectors`, redundant vector tombstones). The finding's parenthetical about `current_batch` is right too: it is an instance attribute never reset (HEAD:349, incremented only at :470), so after a recycle `batch_remaining` is computed over batch 0's range (all non-None), `advance_batch()` fires on the first answer call and jumps to `current_batch+1`.

(2) Is the new behaviour really "resume from the still-unanswered"? Yes, and it is load-bearing, not incidental: `next_batch` (semantic_interpretation.py:403-415) begins `batch = self.unanswered_in_batch()`, and `unanswered_in_batch` is `[i for i in self.batch if self.state[i] == _SENT]` (:416-417); `_GATING`/`_DONE` entries are structurally excluded. `_run_agent`'s own docstring states it (:1013-1014 "the task's queue and states survive, so a recycle continues where the session stopped"). I measured it rather than reading it: a 6-entry task with `batch_size=3`, script `[answer(0,1), raise RateLimitError, answer(2), answer(3,4,5)]`, driven through the real `_run_agent` with `asyncio.sleep` stubbed, gives turns `[c0,c1,c2] → retry[c2] → RECYCLE → [c2,c3,c4] → retry[c3,c4]` and `written` containing each of the six exactly once. c0 and c1 are neither re-asked nor re-written. Under HEAD the post-recycle turn would have been the fixed batch-0 prompt, i.e. c0,c1,c2 again.

(3) Is the difference already covered by one of §15.11's three exceptions? No. The three are: each batch is a turn; every write is a task of the group (a failed write now fails the run); and the correction's write is no longer synchronous with the tool reply. "Each batch is a turn" is a statement about turn structure and does not entail anything about which entries a post-recycle batch contains — one could restructure to one-turn-per-batch and still re-send batch 0. So §15.11:1522's "Behaviour equals today's with three exceptions" is literally false, and §15.11 is the step-3 acceptance criterion the scope names.

The one place I can push back is the finding's own count: the bullet is short by MORE than one. §15.4 (plan:1052-1073) itself lists changes to exactly the handlers §15.11 is summarising, and none of them appears in §15.11 either: the throttle sleeps changed from HEAD's fixed `asyncio.sleep(1200)` / `asyncio.sleep(2)` (HEAD:820, :825) to `1200 ± 60` and `min(2 * 2**throttled, 60) × U(0.5,1.5)` (:1041-1049) — a run that is rate-limited repeatedly now backs off to ~60 s instead of hammering every 2 s, which is plainly observable — and the recursion (`return await _run_agent(...)`, HEAD:822/827/841/862) became a `while True` `continue`, so HEAD's stack growth under a long throttle is gone. So the honest repair is not "add a fourth clause" but "stop claiming exhaustiveness in that sentence".

Note also that the plan is not silent on the resume itself — §5.3 "Recycle paths" (plan:277-281) and §15.4's closing "Recycle:" paragraph (plan:1089-1091) both prescribe it, and §10 already demands the test for it ("a fake driver raising `RateLimitError` mid-turn with part of the batch answered — after the recycle every entry ends non-`None`, none interpreted twice, none lost", plan:677-680), which `test_poisoned_session_recycles_a_fresh_driver_and_keeps_answers` (test_interpretation_driver.py:236-251) pins on the poisoned-session arm. So this is narrowly a false exhaustiveness claim in one sentence of §15.11, not a hole in the design or the tests — which is exactly the "minor" the finding claims. The code is right; the acceptance sentence is wrong.
